newsitem.title: UK: London gold stretches gains at afternoon fix.
newsitem.headline: London gold stretches gains at afternoon fix.

text.p: Gold extended overnight gains on Friday afternoon following fresh buying after New York opened, dealers said.
But dealers and market analysts said the bounce was to be expected as the gold had become seriously oversold as it plunged to 12-year lows last week.
Gold was fixed at $324.20 per ounce up from $323.45 this morning and $319.40 on Thursday afternoon.
Friday's have been the highest fixings since immediately before the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves during the previous six months.
The subsequent price fall was driven by the investment funds massively extending existing short positions in anticipation of prices reaching levels under $300.00.
But that sentiment has dissipated this week after physical buying provided a price base between $315.00 and $318.00.
"The bulls are jumping for joy and forecasting $330.00 per ounce. That might be possible but $340 and $350 look less likely," said market analyst Ted Arnold at Merrill Lynch.
Gold reached a high of $325.70 during the Asian trading day but came off in choppy trade near the close leaving some dealers expecting it to settle in a $323.50-$318.00 range.
"Until it is above the 1993 low ($326.10 fix) the market will still be selling into rallies," said bullion analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland.
A break through $325.00 and the next resistance at $326.60 would be needed to take gold to higher levels. Some interim support should be available at $322.50, technical analysts said.
Smith noted that a significant resistance would be the 50-day moving average just under $340.00.
Short term lease rates have fallen reflecting increased market liquidity as fund short positions were covered.
The implied one month rate was 2.15 per cent on Friday down from 2.62 on Wednesday. The three month rate was also trimmed to 2.03 percent from 2.21 percent.
"We will see just how the open intetst has come down when the Comex figures come out tonight," said Smith.
The other precious metals were also firmer. Silver was up six cents at $4.26/$4.28, platinum was $3.40 up at $405.00/$408.00 and palladium was at $180.00/$183.00, up $5.00.
The platinum group metals were firmer on doubts about the pace of Russian deliveries to Japan after a six-month delay
